correctness.rationale: The three projections are Frobenius-orthogonal. One- and two-coordinate inclusion probabilities derive the covariance C, whose exact eigenvalues and affine-hull rank are computed. Every matching vertex has squared projection lengths equal to each positive eigenvalue times its eigenspace dimension, giving Mahalanobis distance exactly d. For arbitrary containing ellipsoid A centered c, the averaged vertex constraint and determinant AM–GM force det A>=d^d det C, with equality only at c=mean and A=dC. Saturated ranks, multiplicities, volume and anisotropy follow explicitly. A standalone exact-rational enumeration tested 44 parameter profiles and 7,925 matching vertices; it is corroboration only.

value.rationale: The rank-k assignment polytope is a natural complete family spanning simplices, partially supported matchings and Birkhoff polytopes. The exact global best enclosing ellipsoid in the specified Euclidean metric, all principal axes and their multiplicities, intrinsically lower-dimensional boundary cases, full contact set, and exact volume are substantive geometric invariants not obtainable from the existing facet/dimension tables. The sharp square-family anisotropy maximum immediately before saturation and its abrupt loss of two representation modes at saturation explain a genuine metric transition. This is not merely an arbitrary numerical instance; it is an infinite-family classification useful in geometric conditioning and bounding assignment relaxations. No downstream consequence is assumed.
